  CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  AUGUST 14, 2018

Manager’s Office, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates.

City Council Members Present: Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

AUGUST 14, 2018
   ***
At 7:09 p.m., the COUNCIL reconvened in open session in the City Council Chamber, 4045 Palos
Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, CA.
  ***

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

MAYOR HUFF led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present: City Manager Doug Prichard
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer
  Assistant to the City Manager Alexa Davis
  Community Services Director Andy Clark
  City Clerk Heidi Luce

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

NONE.

  The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority
  consent of the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE ITEMS A-N AS PRESENTED BELOW.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

  Council will be waived and all such ordinances and resolutions will be read by title only.

  APPROVED.

AUGUST 14, 2018

  APPROVED AS PRESENTED.

C.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF JULY 10, 2018

  APPROVED AS PRESENTED.

D.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS – JULY AND AUGUST 2018

  APPROVED WARRANTS 60325 THROUGH 60379 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $304,440.12; AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 070118 THROUGH 070518;
  60175 THROUGH 60183; 60176 (VOID); AND 60211 THROUGH 60314 IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $626,933.66 FOR A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT OF $931,373.78 WITH

E.  JUNE 2018 SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
AUGUST 14, 2018
 L.  NOTICE OF COMPLETION FOR WORK PERFORMED BY ALL AMERICAN ASPHALT FOR

  ACCEPTED THE 2017-18 STREET RESURFACING PROJECT AS COMPLETE;
  AUTHORIZED THE CITY CLERK TO FILE A NOTICE OF COMPLETION FOR THE
  PROJECT WITH THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY REGISTRAR-RECORDER’S
  OFFICE; AND DIRECTED STAFF TO RELEASE THE 5% CONSTRUCTION

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

City Manager Prichard read Resolution 2430 by title.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

Susan Cordone, California Water Service Company, provided an update on the status and
progression of the Palos Verdes Peninsula Water Reliability Project.

MAYOR HUFF expressed appreciation for Cal Water’s diligence and responsiveness during this
major construction project.

In response to MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL’S inquiry regarding the status of the agreement with
PV Transit to provided shuttle service to and from Dapplegray Elementary during the project,
Assistant City Manager Grammer commented that officials with Dapplegray Elementary School
and PVPUSD decided not to pursue this option but rather will be promoting the use of carpools
and the “Walking School Bus.”

COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN also expressed appreciation for Cal Water’s professionalism in
handling this project thus far. He also reiterated his previous request that Cal Water remain
transparent when the times comes to determine the cost allocation for this project and to ensure
there is a fair allocation and apportionment of the expenditures related to this project.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

NONE.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
AUGUST 14, 2018
 8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  FIRST AMENDMENT TO MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING – COORDINATED
  INTEGRATED MANAGEMENT PROGRAM (CIMP)

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the First Amendment to the
  Memorandum of Understanding between the Los Angeles County Flood Control District,
  the County of Los Angeles and the cities of Rancho Palos Verdes, Palos Verdes Estates,
  Rolling Hills and Rolling Hills Estates regarding the administration and cost sharing for
  implementing the Coordinated Integrated Monitoring Program (CIMP) for the Peninsula
  CIMP Agencies (CIMP MOU).

  Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda material.) He
  noted that this amendment includes the additional cost for conducting the required
  bacteria shoreline monitoring that had previously been undertaken by Los Angeles
  County Sanitation District. He stated that Rolling Hills Estates’ share of the cost for the
  monitoring will increase by approximately $14,000 this year and $11,000 for the three
  subsequent years of the agreement; and that these funds were included in the budget
  in anticipation of this requirement.

  In response to MAYOR HUFF’S inquiry as to why the County Sanitation District is no
  longer required to conduct the monitoring, Assistant City Manager Grammer
  commented that his understanding it is because they are currently meeting their
  required threshold.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN expressed his frustration with these requirements in
  that they are not ultimately solving the problem. COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN
  suggested that it may be appropriate to convene another meeting between the South
  Bay Cities and State legislators to discuss this matter.

  COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE THE FIRST AMENDMENT TO THE
  MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING BETWEEN THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY
  FLOOD CONTROL DISTRICT, THE COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES AND THE CITIES
  OF RANCHO PALOS VERDES, PALOS VERDES ESTATES, ROLLING HILLS AND
  ROLLING HILLS ESTATES REGARDING THE ADMINISTRATION AND COST
  SHARING  FOR  IMPLEMENTING  THE  COORDINATED  INTEGRATED
  MONITORING PROGRAM (CIMP) FOR THE PENINSULA CIMP AGENCIES (CIMP
  MOU).

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  2018 COMMISSION/COMMITTEE ATTENDANCE REPORT

  Recommendation: That the City Council discuss this matter; provide direction to staff if
  necessary; and receive and file this report.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
AUGUST 14, 2018
   City Clerk Luce provided a staff report (as per agenda material.)

  MAYOR HUFF noted that since the last meeting, staff contacted some of the
  representatives with attendance issues; and in at least one instance it was a simply a
  communication issue that has been resolved. She suggested that a letter be sent to all
  Commissioners and Committee Members reminding them of the importance of regular
  attendance and participation in meetings.

  Following brief discussion, the following action was taken:

  DIRECTED STAFF TO WORK WITH THE MAYOR TO PREPARE LETTERS TO BE
  SENT TO THE COMMISSIONERS AND COMMITTEE MEMBERS REMINDING
  EACH OF THE IMPORTANCE OF REGULAR ATTENDANCE AND PARTICIPATION
  IN THE SCHEDULED MEETINGS. THE REPORT WAS RECEIVED AND FILED.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

A.  AMENDMENTS TO LEGAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH BURKE, WILLIAMS &
  SORENSEN, LLP AND APPOINTMENT OF KANE THUYEN AS ASSISTANT CITY ATTORNEY

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) approve the amended Legal Services
  Agreement between the City of Rolling Hills Estates and Burke, Williams & Sorensen,
  LLP; and 2) appoint Kane Thuyen as Assistant City Attorney.

  City Manager Prichard provided a staff report (as per agenda material.)

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE THE AMENDED LEGAL SERVICES
  AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS ESTATES AND BURKE,
  WILLIAMS & SORENSEN, LLP; AND APPOINT KANE THUYEN AS ASSISTANT
  CITY ATTORNEY.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS:

  This item provides the opportunity for Members of the City Council to provide information
  and reports to other Members of the City Council and/or the public on any issues or activities
  of currently active Council Committees, ad hoc committees, regional or state-wide
  governmental associations, special districts and/or joint powers authorities and their
  various committees on which Members of the City Council might serve or have an interest,
  which are not otherwise agendized.

A.  UPDATE ON WASTE NEGOTIATIONS FOR RESIDENTIAL AND COMMERCIAL SOLID
  WASTE, RECYCLABLE MATERIALS AND ORGANIC WASTE COLLECTION SERVICES
  (COUNCILMEMBERS ZERUNYAN AND SCHMITZ)

  Recommendation: That the City Council receive and file this report.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
AUGUST 14, 2018
   Assistant to the City Manager Davis provided an update on the negotiations with Waste
  Management for the City’s waste collection services (as per agenda material.) She further
  reviewed the proposed modifications which include changes to greenwaste and manure
  collection noting that the complete contract will be brought before the City Council for
  consideration at its meeting of September 11, 2018 with an effective date of October 1,
  2018.

  In response to MAYOR HUFF regarding the length of time the contract negotiations have
  taken and the option to go out to bid, COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN and
  COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ explained the process which included a complete analysis
  of the data related to the service provided, noting that the quality of the service provided
  to residents is unparalleled.

  In response to MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL regarding the proposed rate increase,
  Assistant to the City Manager Davis noted that a rate freeze has been in place since
  2015-16 and the proposed residential rate increase for year one equates to $1.85-$2.54
  per month and year three equates to $0.85-$1.23per month. COUNCILMEMBER
  ZERUNYAN further explained the rationale behind the rate increase.

  In response to COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN regarding the option of adding
  “bagster” service for construction waste, Assistant to the City Manager service explained
  that the service will not be added to the City’s contract but residents will be able to
  purchase the bags at a retail location and schedule pick up by Waste Management.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL RECEIVE AND FILE THIS REPORT.

  Hearing no objection, MAYOR HUFF so ordered.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS:

  This item provides the opportunity for Members of the City Council to request information on
  currently pending projects and/or issues of public concern, direct that an item be agendized
  for future consideration and/or make announcements of interest to the public.

A.  LEAGUE OF CALIFORNIA CITIES – 2018 ANNUAL CONFERENCE RESOLUTIONS
  PACKET

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL provided an overview of Resolution 1 which was put forward
  by the City of Beverly Hills suggesting that the League put forward a ballot measure
  protecting local authority; and Resolution 2 which seeks to allow local governments to
  regulate certain rodenticides.

  Discussion ensued concerning the importance of preserving local authority with the City
  Council concurring that it would be worthwhile to support the League’s efforts to preserve
  local authority. Further discussion ensued concerning the importance of responsible
  rodenticide use and the difficulty cities would have in regulating rodenticides with the City
  Council concurring that such enforcement should be left to other agencies.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  7
AUGUST 14, 2018
   Following discussion, the following action was authorized:

  AUTHORIZED SUPPORT OF RESOLUTION 1 PROPOSED BY THE CITY OF
  BEVERLY HILLS PERTAINING TO A BALLOT MEASURE AND/OR
  CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT THAT WOULD FURTHER STRENGTHEN
  LOCAL DEMOCRACY AND AUTHORITY.

B.  AUTHORIZATION TO ATTEND THE CALIFORNIA CONTRACT CITIES ASSOCIATION FALL
  EDUCATIONAL SUMMIT – OCTOBER 5-7, 2018

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL AUTHORIZE ALL COUNCILMEMBERS TO ATTEND
  THE CALIFORNIA CONTRACT CITIES ASSOCIATION FALL EDUCATIONAL
  SUMMIT.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

  Councilmember Zerunyan expressed his interest in attending the event.

**OTHER REPORTS**

MAYOR HUFF noted that the Hills Are Alive Race was a very well organized, well attended event
and thanked the Park & Activities Commission and staff for their efforts in making the event
successful.

MAYOR HUFF also commented on the National Night Out events noting that there were several
events this year and the participants seemed to enjoy them.

COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN noted that the Californian Contract Cities Annual meeting
hosted by the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department will be held on Wednesday, August 15
at the L.A. County Arboretum and encouraged the COUNCIL to attend if available.

13.  CLOSED SESSION (TAKEN OUT OF ORDER – SEE ABOVE)

14.  ADJOURNMENT

  At 8:20 p.m. MAYOR HUFF adjourned the City Council meeting to an adjourned meeting
  scheduled for Monday, August 20, 2018 beginning at 5:30 p.m. at City Hall, 4045 Palos
